note:
ARCHITECTURE/CONTENT ISSUE: Kentridge still assembles significant character runtime/presentation behavior in scene-specific code, and Madeline is still represented by a placeholder even though a production Madeline model has recently been added. Bring the Kentridge character stack onto the shared game-owned character pipeline, then replace Madeline's placeholder with the real asset through that pipeline.

1. Shared character ownership. Audit Assets/Scenes/Kentridge and KentridgePlayableSlice. KentridgePlayableSlice currently constructs/ticks character integration directly (including CharacterMotor/ActorHost wiring) and the scene assembly directly depends on VoxelEngine.Characters.Runtime. The scene may choose characters, spawn locations, scenario/cutscene parameters, and presentation settings, but reusable character behavior must be owned by the game/character modules, not by scene-specific code.

Use the canonical Game composition seams (including IKentridgeCampaignActorHost) and provide a reusable game-owned implementation/composition root for player/NPC construction and runtime. Movement/locomotion behavior, animation state/transition decisions, animation playback and retargeting policy, model/rig binding, character interaction behavior, and reusable visual/root/foot alignment belong in shared Game/character code. KentridgeCutsceneFootGrounding and any other scene-local actor/model adaptation logic must be audited; generic behavior should move/generalize into the shared character pipeline rather than continue as a Kentridge-only workaround. If the game layer does not expose a primitive/capability Kentridge needs, add it there instead of creating a parallel scene-local path. Do not solve this by adding a Kentridge-only Animator Controller or duplicating animation logic beside the model.

2. Production Madeline presentation. Replace the current Madeline placeholder used by Kentridge with the recently added real/production Madeline model asset. Locate and document the authoritative asset as part of the fix, then bind it through the shared game character presentation pipeline. Preserve Madeline's existing story/cutscene identity and gameplay role while changing only her visual/model implementation.

Acceptance:
- Scene-specific Kentridge code no longer owns reusable player/NPC movement, locomotion, animation decisions, actor construction, model binding/retargeting, or generic rig/foot-alignment logic.
- Kentridge obtains its authoritative character host/runtime through reusable Assets/Game character/composition modules and feeds that host into the existing campaign composition API.
- Kentridge may still configure spawn positions, character identities, scenario/cutscene parameters, and presentation-only scene settings.
- Madeline resolves to the real production model, not the placeholder, through the shared game character pipeline.
- Verify the Madeline asset's humanoid/rig/avatar setup, materials, scale/orientation, root-motion policy, collider/avatar alignment, foot placement, idle/locomotion/expected action/cutscene animations, and normal gameplay interactions.
- The opening cutscene and its handoff to gameplay still function correctly with real Madeline.
- Add focused regressions proving Kentridge character behavior comes through the shared game systems and that Madeline resolves to the intended production model rather than the placeholder.

Scope: this issue requires the Madeline art swap only. Other placeholder character models may remain unless changing them is strictly necessary to establish the shared reusable pipeline.
